# Strict integer interpolation for a concave continuous buffer

This extends the archived ordinary theorem
candidate 9afb6a8708a420d7 to the actual
finite-epsilon H buffer. The new point is that a pure base tilt leaves
the buffer unchanged. The section trimming lemma and its sharp
one-dimensional width bound are ordinary, fully stated below.

## 1. Statement and precise properness hypotheses

Let C be a compact convex body in R times R^d, d>=1, with finitely
many positive sampled fibers and total mixed d-volume M>0.
Let f:C->[0,infinity) be concave and continuous and let Gamma be a
positive continuous homogeneous norm of the continuous normal.
For epsilon>=0 define the buffered through-mark caps by

    a(Z-z)+u·(X-x)>=-epsilon f(z,x)Gamma(u),   u nonzero,

together with ordinary closed pure-base caps. Let D_epsilon(z,x)
be the infimum of their mixed volumes, without dividing by M.

Let Y_0=(z_0,x_0), Y_1=(z_1,x_1) have integer bases z_0<z_1 and
positive depths. Let p be an integer strictly between them, and
Y=(1-t)Y_0+tY_1 over p. Assume that if

    D_epsilon(Y)=min(D_epsilon(Y_0),D_epsilon(Y_1)),

there is an attaining nonvertical cap at Y whose own cut at Y is
proper, and whose own cuts at both endpoint sources are proper once
it propagates to them. Then

    D_epsilon(Y)>min(D_epsilon(Y_0),D_epsilon(Y_1)).     (1)

For the NEW H problem in its stated small-epsilon compact class,
all deepest marks have uniform own balls and all their through-mark
continuous cuts are proper; finite continuous-cap attainment and the
pure-base reserve were proved separately. Hence the displayed
properness premise holds whenever the endpoints and Y are deepest.

In particular, the actual H deepest bases in one integer dimension
are either a singleton or two adjacent integers. A full-rank deepest
source interval with a relative-interior integer witness cannot occur,
at finite epsilon and in any continuous dimension.

## 2. Equality propagates one actual cap to both endpoints

For a fixed nonvertical normal N=(a,u), write its through-mark
threshold as

    b_N(W)=N·W-epsilon f(W)Gamma(u).

Concavity of f gives

    b_N(Y)<=(1-t)b_N(Y_0)+t b_N(Y_1).

Thus buffered depth has convex superlevel sets: if both endpoints
have depth at least A, their N-cap thresholds are below the right
A-quantile for every N, and so is the intermediate threshold.
The ordinary pure-base conditions have the same convex-superlevel
property. Therefore D_epsilon(Y)>=A, where A is the endpoint minimum.

Suppose equality holds and choose the stated attaining nonvertical
proper cap H={N·w>=b}. Its mass is A. Properness at Y makes its upper
tail strictly decreasing near b, and hence any threshold greater
than b has mass strictly smaller than A. Endpoint depth at least A
therefore implies b_N(Y_i)<=b for both endpoints.
Concavity also gives

    b=b_N(Y)<=(1-t)b_N(Y_0)+t b_N(Y_1)<=b.

All inequalities are equalities. Both endpoint thresholds equal b;
the same cap H has mass A and minimizes buffered cap mass at both
endpoints. In particular both endpoint depths equal A.

No centroid or body variation is used here. The cap remains a single
closed ambient halfspace.

## 3. Its actual section sequence and optional endpoint weights

Normalize |u|=1 and write the section plane as u·X=b-a z.
Let s_z be its (d-1)-volume within K_z; for d=1 let s_z=1 when the
section is nonempty and zero otherwise.
For this section calculation, first truncate C to the interval from
the smallest to the largest positive-volume integer fiber. Positive
sampled fibers form a consecutive interval by convexity, and the
discarded fibers have zero mixed d-volume. Thus the truncation changes
neither cap masses nor the endpoint minima. All remaining sampled
fibers are positive. Retain the ORIGINAL f restricted to this set;
do not recompute a body-tied energy or volume profile on the truncation.

The sections form a convex family after the affine chart
(z,xi)->(z,xi+(b-a z)u), xi in u-perp. Consequently, for d>=2,
s_z^(1/(d-1)) is concave on the real section projection. The positive
sampled s_z form a log-concave sequence at consecutive integer
indices. For d=1 they are all one.

Only the two extreme bases of the real section projection can have
nonproper cuts. To check this directly, choose one proper source
base and extend a segment through any interior projection point
slightly beyond it within that projection. The continuous margin's
fiber minimum is convex in the base and its maximum is concave.
Their strict opposite signs at the source therefore give strict
opposite signs at every such interior point. Supporting endpoint
sections of zero area contribute no weight.

At a fixed source endpoint Y_e, perturb ONLY the base normal:

    a -> a+h,       b -> b+h z_e.

The continuous normal, Gamma(u), source and buffer are all fixed.
At a proper section the mass derivative is (z-z_e)s_z. At a
supporting endpoint its two one-sided contributions are zero and
(z-z_e)s_z in the appropriate order. These are actual shell
derivatives, including inside and outside supporting incidences.

The cap is minimizing at Y_e. Its left derivative is nonpositive and
its right derivative nonnegative. Interpolating the two one-sided
linear expressions yields effective weights with

    s'_z=s_z at proper sections,
    0<=s'_z<=s_z at supporting endpoints,
    sum_z(z-z_e)s'_z=0.                                (2)

Only the two extreme weights may vary. The total weight is positive
because the source sections are proper. Thus both z_0 and z_1 are
centroids of the same positive log-concave sequence, with just those
two endpoint weights allowed to decrease.

## 4. The trimming-mean interval has length at most one

Let w_0,...,w_L be positive and log-concave, L>=2. Hold the interior
weights fixed and let each endpoint weight range from zero to its
given value. The possible means lie between

    m_- =sum_(i=0)^(L-1)i w_i /sum_(i=0)^(L-1)w_i,
    m_+ =sum_(i=1)^L i w_i /sum_(i=1)^L w_i.

Compare the probability laws on 0,...,L-1 proportional respectively
to w_i and to w_(i+1). Their likelihood ratio is nonincreasing, since
w_(i+1)/w_i is nonincreasing. Explicitly, the numerator of the
second mean minus the first is

    sum_(i<j)(j-i)[w_(j+1)w_i-w_(i+1)w_j]<=0.

The second mean is m_+-1. Hence m_+-m_-<=1.

Equation (2) puts both distinct source indices into this same interval.
Their integer difference is at least two, a contradiction. This proves
(1) and the H adjacency conclusion.

## 5. Scope and effect on the recent one-group branch

The new H hypotheses supply all the required properness and
attainment facts, so the adjacency consequence is unconditional
within that already attained small-epsilon framework.
It uses no constant envelope scale, smoothness, radial symmetry,
projective measure replacement, or chosen supporting allocation.

Consequently the actual occupied-interval hypotheses in
candidate d8f7a4409a9bdcfe
are empty in this framework, although its conditional minorant
implication remains mathematically correct. The independently derived
one-group quota/envelope exclusion reaches the same conclusion.

For n>=2, optional section weights can occur at many boundary lattice
bases, and one-dimensional likelihood-ratio order no longer applies.
No multidimensional trimming-width or parity theorem is inferred.
